item.lead_in: The affected protein normally performs which cellular function?
item.tested_construct: Desmoplakin is a desmosomal structural protein that anchors intermediate filaments to the desmosomal plaque, enabling mechanical coupling between cardiomyocytes. DSP variants can cause a left-dominant arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with myocardial fibrosis, ventricular arrhythmias, and episodic myocardial injury.

blind_audit.rationale: BAG3 is a stress-responsive cochaperone that interacts with Hsp70-family chaperones and participates in chaperone-assisted selective autophagy/protein-quality control. Disruption of this proteostasis network in mechanically stressed cardiomyocytes can cause dilated cardiomyopathy. Strongest alternative resolved: Desmosomal disease can cause cardiomyopathy, but the stem identifies BAG3 and its Hsc70/Hsp70 interaction; BAG3 is a cochaperone/proteostasis protein rather than a desmosomal adhesion component.
